SNACS review rules and exceptions

Each target has a scene role and a lexical function. The function is typically an ancestor of the role, but can differ; preserve both labels when examples show a construal. Use context and guideline definitions rather than treating surface forms as fixed labels.

Genitives and possessives: identify the relation conveyed by the possessor form. An organization framed through its members can be Org;Gestalt (e.g. Stuart's ethical strategies). An organization noun used as possessor can be OrgMember;Possessor (e.g. our business will reap rewards). A possessive pronoun modifying a person or thing can be Agent;Gestalt in context (e.g. your contributions; their service), while ordinary ownership remains Possessor;Possessor (e.g. your money). A possessor expressing a social relation can be SocialRel;Gestalt (e.g. my friend). Genitives of an attribute or quality can be Gestalt;Gestalt (e.g. ethical strategies).

Of phrases: amount/number + of + item can be QuantityItem;Whole (e.g. each of you). Of after an adjective of emotion/evaluation can be Stimulus;Topic (e.g. proud of contributions). Of indicating the force behind an event can be Force;Force (e.g. reap the rewards of a program). Of describing material can be Stuff;Stuff (e.g. pieces of wood). Of after kind/variety can mark Species;Species.

Temporal expressions: since introducing a time point can be Time;Time. Throughout a time span is Duration;Duration. After can mark Time;Time when locating an event relative to another event. In a clock or calendar time expression can be Time;Time.

To phrases: a verb's addressee/recipient can be Recipient;Goal (e.g. recommend to anyone). To marking a destination is Goal;Goal; an infinitive of purpose can be Purpose;Purpose.

Other useful distinctions: with can mark Theme in a verb's complement (e.g. bother with this; start off with). For in an intended-use or search complement can mark Theme; for dinner can mark Purpose. Like used for resemblance/comparison is ComparisonRef;ComparisonRef, but complement clauses may have Theme role and ComparisonRef function (e.g. look like they were flooded). Spatial at can be Locus;Locus. Spatial over to a destination can be Goal;Locus.

These patterns are example-backed, not unconditional rules. Resolve ambiguity from the construction and sentence context; retain distinct role and function labels where warranted.
